title: Empirical quantization regression matrix — int8/int4/awq comparison
body:
Executive summary:

This note contains the empirical regression matrix from our internal onboarding runs comparing FP16 (baseline) against three quantized variants: 8-bit dynamic (int8-dyn), 4-bit AWQ (int4-awq), and 4-bit GPTQ (int4-gptq). The goal: characterize quality deltas by slice and produce decision rules for rolling quantized model variants to hosted/dedicated.

Key findings (high level):
- Median quality deltas vs FP16 on the primary metric (slice-weighted EM/ROUGE-L depending on workload) are: int8-dyn -0.4%, int4-awq -2.1%, int4-gptq -2.9%.
- Variation across slices is large: some slices (short instructive prompts, generic summarization) tolerate int4 fairly well (<1.5% delta), while others (code generation, multi-step math reasoning, long-context retrieval) see regressions >6% for int4-gptq.
- AWQ performed better than GPTQ on code-oriented slices (median +0.9% relative to GPTQ), we hypothesize clustering-friendly weight distributions in those layers. GPTQ tends to be more consistent on arithmetic/mathematical reasoning slices.
- Int8-dyn is low-risk across all tested slices; we recommend broad rollout with automated monitoring.

Experiment matrix and methodology:
- Baseline: FP16 model checkpoint used in production candidate (model v3.1.0).
- Quant variants:
  * int8-dyn: bitsandbytes 8-bit dynamic conversion, per-tensor scaling, post-training.
  * int4-awq: AWQ v0.3 pipeline, per-channel scales where applicable with outlier-clipping 0.02.
  * int4-gptq: GPTQ-lite v1.2, layerwise second-order correction, per-tensor scales.
- Hardware: A100-80GB for FP16 and int8 runs; T4/GA100 cluster for int4 runs where we wanted representative latency/cost tradeoffs.
- Eval harness: reproducible runner in git repo (see linked_artifacts). Each run used identical prompt seeds and temperature=0 for deterministic tasks; sampling metrics controlled where applicable.
- Statistical testing: paired bootstrap on prompt-level scores (5k resamples) to compute 95% confidence intervals and p-values for deltas. We mark regressions as statistically significant if p<0.01 and median delta <= -0.5% on the slice primary metric.

Prompt sets and slices (what we grouped and why):
We built prompt slices to reflect product-mapped risk categories:
- Summarization-short: single-paragraph news summarization; metric: ROUGE-L.
- Summarization-long: multi-paragraph doc->summary; metric: ROUGE-L.
- Instruction-small: single-turn instruction-following; metric: task-specific exact-match / classification F1.
- Multi-turn-chat: conversational context >4 turns; metrics: turn-level BLEU + conversation turn coherency score.
- Code-generation: Python function generation from spec; metric: test-case pass-rate (unit tests).
- Math-reasoning: multi-step arithmetic/algebra; metric: exact-match on final numeric answer.
- Retrieval-augmented: prompt + retrieved docs; metric: combined F1 + citation accuracy.
- Long-context: >8k token prompts (simulated); metric: chunked ROUGE + hallucination rate.
Each slice contains 800-2,000 prompts drawn from internal evaluation library (mix of public bench subsets and in-house customer-style prompts).

Results (slice highlights and regression matrix commentary):
Rather than paste the full 800x4 table, below are distilled takeaways and representative numbers (median delta vs FP16 on primary metric):
- Summarization-short: int8 -0.2%, int4-awq -0.7% (p=0.04), int4-gptq -1.1% (p=0.003).
- Summarization-long: int8 -0.6%, int4-awq -2.0% (p<0.001), int4-gptq -2.7% (p<0.001).
- Instruction-small: int8 -0.1%, int4-awq -0.9% (p=0.02), int4-gptq -1.3% (p=0.007).
- Multi-turn-chat: int8 -0.5%, int4-awq -3.8% (p<0.001), int4-gptq -4.5% (p<0.001).
- Code-generation: int8 -0.4%, int4-awq -1.6% (p=0.005), int4-gptq -2.5% (p=0.0004); note AWQ shows smaller delta vs GPTQ here.
- Math-reasoning: int8 -0.3%, int4-awq -3.1% (p<0.001), int4-gptq -1.7% (p=0.001) — GPTQ unexpectedly outperforms AWQ on this slice.
- Retrieval-augmented: int8 -0.5%, int4-awq -2.4% (p<0.001), int4-gptq -3.5% (p<0.001).
- Long-context: int8 -0.7%, int4-awq -6.2% (p<0.001), int4-gptq -7.1% (p<0.001).

Pairwise regression matrix (conceptual):
We computed pairwise deltas for every slice and quant pair (FP16 vs int8, FP16 vs int4-awq, FP16 vs int4-gptq, and int4-awq vs int4-gptq). The matrix shows:
- Int8 cells are mostly near-zero with narrow CIs; safe for rollout.
- Int4 cells have wider spread: AWQ vs GPTQ differences depend on slice (code favoring AWQ, math favoring GPTQ).
- The int4-awq vs int4-gptq differential median ranges +/-1.2% depending on slice, with p-values often <0.05 where differences exceed 1.5%.

Anomalies and root-cause hypotheses:
- Long-context worst-case regressions correlate with attention-kernel quantization noise in the KV projection layers; spike in token-level logprob drops at position >1024. Hypothesis: per-tensor scaling insufficient for long attention contexts — consider per-channel + clipped outlier handling in KV layers.
- Code slice: AWQ handles large low-rank weight blocks better due to its blockwise clustering quantization; GPTQ’s layerwise second-order correction still loses some precision on embeddings used for symbol table generation.
- Math slice: GPTQ’s second-order correction stabilizes arithmetic-sensitive linear layers; AWQ without second-order steps is more lossy for chained reasoning.

Operational recommendations and rollout rules:
1) Int8-dyn: approve automatic rollout to Hosted and Dedicated as the default cost-saving tier with continuous monitoring.
   - Alert thresholds: per-route median delta <= -1.0% triggers auto-rollback; per-route tail 95th percentile latency/regression triggers immediate investigation.
2) Int4 variants: only roll out to non-critical routes or internal beta cohorts. For customer-facing routes, require per-slice gate checks:
   - No statistical regression (p<0.01) on any customer-visible slice with median delta <= -0.5%.
   - Additional manual QA on code/math/long-context slices if any delta > 2%.
3) Mixed-precision strategy: prefer layerwise hybrid (keep FP16 for KV and selected MLP layers) for production int4 deployment; re-evaluate with small canary.
4) Monitoring: add prompt-hash level sampling for slices and a sliding 7-day regression dashboard. Metric telemetry must include token-level logprob delta and unit-test pass-rate for code generation.

Next steps and experiments to close gaps:
- Re-run AWQ with per-channel scaling on KV layers and compare long-context regressions.
- Try GPTQ with a smaller blocksize on embeddings + clustering-aware preconditioning.
- Explore mixed int8/int4: int8 for attention and embedding layers, int4 for MLPs — run an automated sweep on the top-5 regression slices.
- Customer-proxy tests: mirror a small percentage (5%) of production traffic to quantized variants and measure real-world metric drift.

Reproducibility and artifacts:
- Repo and runner: git+ssh://github.com/redwood-inference/quant-eval-harness.git (branch empirical-matrix-2024).
- Artifacts: gs://redwood-inference-ml/quant-evals/empirical-2024-09-18/ contains raw scores, per-prompt deltas (csvs), and the full regression matrix heatmaps (png/html).
- Quick reproduce steps (short):
  1) git clone the repo and checkout branch.
  2) docker build -t quant-eval:empirical .
  3) python run_eval.py --model checkpoint_fp16.pt --variants int8,int4-awq,int4-gptq --slices all --out gs://redwood-inference-ml/quant-evals/empirical-2024-09-18/ --seed 42

Appendix (notes to reviewers):
- This document focuses on empirical median deltas vs FP16; teams that care about hallucination/faithfulness should inspect the raw prompt-level outputs in the artifact bucket.
- We intentionally set a conservative significance threshold; please propose relaxations only with supporting customer risk analysis.
- Open questions: best practice for per-customer slice weighting; how to automate per-route mixed-precision recommendations.

Authors and next reviewers: Maya Chen (owner), Arjun Patel (quant pipeline), Lena Gómez (eval bench), Tomás Ruiz (SRE perf). Please comment inline on the branch PR; plan to freeze a recommended rule-set for int8 by 2024-10-01 and a measured int4 canary policy by 2024-12-15.
